title: Optimization-Guided Diffusion for Interactive Scene Generation

control_signal.value: Explicit goal points for one or more target agents (via inpainting mask) for controllability; for adversarial generation, a designated attacker vehicle against the ego.

control_mechanism.value: Training-free: each reverse diffusion step is re-anchored by KL-bounded constrained optimisation in clean space, with a two-phase noise schedule; adversarial case is a game-theoretic optimisation in distribution space approximating Nash equilibria.

base_model.value: Applied without retraining on the pretrained Nexus diffusion scene generator (trained on nuPlan), giving Nexus-Omega; also applied to VBD.

datasets.value: nuPlan (base model training), Waymo zero-shot, Waymo Open Sim Agents validation set.

metrics.value: Distributional JSD (nearest-agent distance, lateral/angular deviation, speed), collision, off-road, kinematic feasibility, Scene Valid Rate, WOSAC Realism Meta score; adversarial: TTC, near-collision frame share.

controllability_evidence.value: Goal-conditioned setting: scene valid rate rises from 11.00% (Nexus) to 80.00% (Nexus-Omega), a 69-point gain; collision falls 39 points, off-road 44 points. Free exploration valid rate 32.35% to 72.27% on nuPlan.

stated_limitations.value: Runtime: optimising an 8-second scene takes around 5 seconds. Failure cases include autoregressive drift in stationary agents and overlaps already present in initial states.

notes: Plug-in sampler on an existing generator. Goal-conditioned control is also supported by the base model's inpainting; OMEGA improves validity while following it.
